_about: The glory hub (plan 7.6f), built the way love, righteousness and hope are: the rows are defined by the Hebrew and Greek, a noun row by the words standing in the noun's own phrase or verse (or, where a loose rule took verses that do not show the label, by hand), a verb row by the verb's frame or by hand, and a verse sits in every row it fits (match: all). The review panel flagged glory low (committee-flags.json): 'the glory of the LORD' and 'the glory of Christ' in one row would read as asserting one glory; the Hebrew כָּבוֹד and the Greek δόξα are different words and are marked so. Taken so: each phrase is its own row, as written; the persons are rows by hand; no row equates two of them. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/glory.json. Panel round (11 fixes, 'ship after fixes'): 26 rows. Consolidated from 40 rows to 25(the coordinator's brief rule 8: about 15-25; love has 22): rows that said the same thing were merged and the one- and two-verse rows were folded, every verse kept placed (338 noun verses and 71 verb verses before and after, none left under 'More').

titles.noun: What the text says of glory

_forms_why: g4888 συνδοξάζω (Rom 8:17, 'glorified with Him') has no lexicon entry, so the builder would type it a noun and its verse would stand in the noun rows
_words_why: The concept's own words: כָּבוֹד and δόξα (the Greek Old Testament renders the one by the other) and the verbs of the same families: δοξάζω, ἐνδοξάζομαι, συνδοξάζω and the Hebrew verb כָּבֵד. תִּפְאֶרֶת 'beauty, splendor', יְקָר 'precious', הֶדֶר 'ornament', כְּבוּדָּה, אָדַר, פִּאֵר 'beautify' and ἔνδοξος 'held in honor' are different words the English also calls glory, so they stand in 'others', apart, never as the same word. The card's family list also holds δοκέω 'think' and κενόδοξος 'conceited', which share the root and not the sense.
_sense_why: כָּבוֹד is 'glory' in MACULA 152 times of 200 and 'honor' 34, 'wealth' 5, 'soul' 3, 'riches', 'abundance', 'nobles' once or twice (the Hebrew root כבד is 'be heavy'); the rule keeps it where the verse renders it glory. The verses where it is rendered otherwise are not dropped out of sight: they stand in one row near the end ('Where the English does not say glory'), which holds two kinds side by side with a note naming both -- the Hebrew word in another sense (honor, wealth, riches; 46 verses) and glory in the original that the English renders splendor, pomp or praise (17). The same rule keeps כָּבֵד only where it is 'glorify', 'glorious', 'gain glory' (18 of 106; the rest is 'honor your father', 'heavy', 'hardened') and δοξάζω only where it is 'glorify'.

sense_keep.Isa.22.23: Berean: 'a throne of glory for the house of his father' (MACULA glosses כָּבוֹד 'honor')
sense_keep.Ps.84.11: Berean: 'the LORD gives grace and glory' (MACULA glosses כָּבוֹד 'honor')
sense_keep.Ps.57.8: Berean: 'Awake, my glory!' (MACULA glosses כָּבוֹד 'soul'); panel fix: it prints glory, so it belongs with glory and not in the row of other senses

others._why: Words the English renders 'glory' that are not this concept's own words (as love names φιλέω and חֶסֶד apart). The rows stand on כָּבוֹד and δόξα and their verbs; a different word the English also calls glory is named apart with its verses and never handed over as the same. min_n 100 with min_share .25 means: a word counts when a quarter of its verses are 'glory', whatever their number (הֶדֶר, once, Dan 11:20; תִּפְאֶרֶת about half). Also named there, as the builder finds them: כְּבוּדָּה (Ps 45:13, from the same root as כָּבוֹד), אָדַר, ἐπιφανής, ἔνδοξος.
others.title: Other words translated “glory”

_review: Not yet reviewed. The panel's flag (low): keep 'the glory of the LORD' and 'the glory of Christ' in separate rows as written, and label the Hebrew and Greek words as different. Taken so: the phrase rows ('the glory of the LORD', 'of God') are by the grammar (the very next word); every row about one person (Christ, the Father, the Spirit, the titles and 'the Lord', the doxologies, who glorifies whom) is by hand; no row says the persons' glory is one. Consolidation (40 to 25): the Father, Christ and Spirit rows stay apart, each verse labelled by whom the text names; the Lamb's doxologies (Rev 5:12-13) moved into the Christ row; the two 'who glorifies whom' verb rows are one; the Hebrew and Greek 'glorify' rows stay apart.

rows.label: The glory of the LORD, glory to the LORD; the LORD called glory
rows.note: The Hebrew כָּבוֹד with the LORD's name beside it, kept as written.
rows._add_why: Ps 3:3 ('You, O LORD, are my glory') and Zech 2:5 ('I will be the glory within it') call the LORD the glory itself; the word beside the glory is not the very next lemma. Folded from the one-row 'Called someone's glory' (7 verses), whose other five went to the people row

rows.label: The glory of God, glory to God
rows.note: The text's own phrases, kept as written: Hebrew אֱלֹהִים and Greek θεός are different words, and 'glory to God' (giving it) is not the same claim as 'the glory of God'; both stand here as the text has them.

rows.label: “The glory of the Lord”; “King of glory,” “God of glory,” “Lord of glory,” “Father of glory”
rows.note: Each title as written. Where the Greek says 'the Lord' readers take it of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose; the page does not say whether the titles are one or several, or whose.
rows._why: by hand: a title naming a person is not read by rule. Merged from the phrase row 'the glory of the Lord' (5, by rule) and the titles row (9, by hand) -- both held the no-choice handling of 'the Lord' (2 Cor 3:18 says 'the Lord, who is the Spirit', and also stands in the Spirit row); 1 Cor 2:7 stays out of this row ('the Lord of glory' is the next verse's)

rows.label: The Father named with glory
rows.note: The verses where the text itself names the Father beside glory (John 17: the Son addresses Him). How it relates them is in the verses, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are; kept apart from the Christ and Spirit rows

rows.label: Christ named with glory
rows.note: The verses where the text itself names Christ, Jesus, the Son of Man or the Lamb beside glory (a verse that also names the Father stands in the Father's row as well). How it relates them -- his own glory, glory given to him, glory in him, glory to him -- is in the verses, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand: a rule on Χριστός would take every verse the name stands in and decide for the text what it has not said. The row stands beside the Father's and the Spirit's and the phrase rows above, never merged with them. Rev 5:12-13 (the Lamb) moved in here from the two-verse 'Glory to Christ, to the Lamb' row; Rev 5:13 also stands in the God doxology row because it addresses both

rows.label: The Holy Spirit named with glory
rows.note: The verses where the text itself names the Spirit, or the Spirit of Christ or of glory, beside glory. How it relates them is in the verses, and the page does not choose (2 Cor 3:18 says 'the Lord, who is the Spirit'; 1 Pet 1:11 'the Spirit of Christ'; Eph 3:16 'His Spirit').
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: the verses that name the Spirit beside glory. 2 Cor 3:18 says 'the Lord, who is the Spirit'; the page does not choose among readings of it

rows.label: The glory appears: in the cloud, the fire, the light; seen, shown, revealed
rows._why: by hand, merged from 'Glory with the cloud, the fire and the light' (28) and 'The glory seen, shown, revealed' (34), 60 verses once the overlap is counted: the loose rule (cloud, fire, light, see or appear anywhere in the verse) took 1 Pet 1:7 (gold refined by fire), Eph 1:18, Jer 13:16, Isa 10:16, 1 Tim 3:16 (a hymn: 'seen by angels'), Hos 10:5 and Hag 2:3, so the verses are named. The first four examples were chosen to show each of fire, revealed, seen and shown. Panel fix: Exod 33:22 ('when My glory passes by', Moses hidden in the cleft) added beside 33:18, so the glory shown and the glory that passes by are both here; Exod 33:20 and John 1:18 do not contain the glory word and are not listed

rows.label: The glory fills the house and the earth; it leaves, returns, dwells; among the nations, above the heavens
rows._why: by hand, merged from 'The glory fills the house and the earth; it leaves, returns, dwells' (26) and 'Glory over the earth, among the nations, above the heavens' (23). 'Filled' by rule took Luke 9:31, Phil 1:11 and Phil 4:19; 'earth, nations or heaven' anywhere in the verse took 46 verses, among them Acts 7:55, 1 Tim 3:16 and Ezek 31:18. Hab 2:16 'filled with shame instead of glory' is left to the shame row

rows.label: Glory with honor, majesty, splendor, power, strength

not_verses.Ps.62.7: עֹז here is 'strong' of the rock (my strong rock), not a strength set beside the glory

rows._why: merged from 'Glory and honor, majesty, splendor' (24) and 'Glory and power, strength, might' (23): the same grammar, a companion word in the verse. ἐξουσία stays out (Luke 4:6, Rev 16:9: authority, not power beside glory)

rows.label: “I will not yield My glory to another”; “give glory to the LORD”; “not to us, O LORD, but to Your name be the glory”
rows._why: by hand, its own row so the Hebrew Scriptures are heard on their own terms: Isa 42:8 and 48:11 were by rule in the 'Give glory' row beside John 17:22, which framed them. Panel fix: Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1 were still in that row beside John 17:22, so all four are out of it now (not_verses there) and no John verse is anywhere near this row; the label is the text's own phrases, with no 'alone' (neither Isa 42:12 nor Ps 115:1 says it)

rows.label: “The glory You gave Me”: the Son's prayer (John 17)
rows._why: by hand, from the panel: John 17:22 ('I have given them the glory You gave Me') is out of 'Give glory' and no longer shares a row with an Isaiah or Psalm verse. It stands with the other two verses of the same prayer, where the Son addresses the Father (17:5 and 17:24 also in the Father row, which names Him)

rows.label: Give glory, ascribe glory (to God)

not_verses.Ezek.39.21: שׂים there is 'set, display' My glory among the nations, not a giving of it
not_verses.Isa.42.8: its own row above, so the Hebrew is not framed by the Greek verses here
not_verses.Isa.48.11: its own row above, so the Hebrew is not framed by the Greek verses here
not_verses.Isa.42.12: its own row above (Hebrew Scriptures on their own terms)
not_verses.Ps.115.1: its own row above (Hebrew Scriptures on their own terms)
not_verses.John.17.22: glory given by the Father to the Son, a different action from ascribing it; with its prayer in its own row
not_verses.Luke.4.6: the devil offers 'all their glory'; not ascribing glory to God (in the people row)
not_verses.1Pet.1.21: God raised Christ and gave Him glory; not ascribing glory to God (in the row of suffering and being raised)
not_verses.Ps.84.11: 'the LORD gives grace and glory'; glory given by God, not ascribed to Him (in the row of grace)
not_verses.Isa.35.2: 'the glory of Lebanon will be given to it'; glory given to a land, not ascribed to God (in the LORD and people rows)

rows._why: panel fix: the row held glory ascribed to God and also glory given BY someone TO someone (John 17:22, Luke 4:6, 1 Pet 1:21, Ps 84:11, Isa 35:2); those five are out by not_verses, each placed in the row that fits it

rows.label: Glory to God; to the glory of God; to the praise of His glory
rows._why: by hand, merged from 'To the glory of God, to the praise of His glory' (14 after Isa 48:11 moved out) and 'Glory to God' (9), doxologies whose verse names God: the purpose clauses and the doxologies are the same act, glory ascribed to God. Ps 115:1 is in the Isaiah row

rows.label: “To Him be the glory”
rows.note: The verse says 'Him' or 'whom'; readers take it of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand: the doxologies whose own verse does not settle whom it addresses

rows.label: People and their glory: kings, nations, a land; glory sought, received from people; one called another's glory
rows.note: Where the text speaks of a person's, king's, nation's or land's glory, of seeking or receiving it from people, or calls one person another's glory, as written. 1 Cor 11:7 says the man is the image and glory of God and the woman is the glory of man; 11:15 says a woman's long hair is her glory. The page gives the verses as written and takes no side on how they apply. (Isa 16:14, 17:4, John 12:43 and 1 Thess 2:6 are printed 'splendor' and 'praise' by the Berean; the original word is the glory word.)
rows._why: panel fixes: the first four examples now say 'glory' in the Berean (Matt 6:29, Luke 2:32, Rom 9:4, 1 Cor 11:7); Isa 16:14, 17:4, John 12:43 and 1 Thess 2:6, which print splendor or praise, are last, and no longer also sit in the row of other renderings; Matt 4:8 and Luke 4:6 ('all the kingdoms ... and their glory') added; the 1 Cor 11 note says what each verse says and names no modern debate. By hand, merged from 'The glory of kings, nations, a people, a land, all flesh' (15, rule plus 5 added), 'Seek glory, receive glory' (10) and 'Called someone's glory' (7). Left out of the seeking verses: 2 Pet 1:17, Rev 4:11 and Rev 5:12 (God or Christ receiving glory; they stand in the rows that name them). Ps 3:3 and Zech 2:5 went to the LORD row. Ps 24:7-10, Ps 96:3 and 1 Sam 6:5, which the old rule took and `not_verses` had to remove, are not here

rows.label: Glory exchanged; glory and shame
rows._why: by hand: the exchange verses and the verses that set glory against shame or dishonor. Kept as its own row (8): the card's own theme 'They exchanged their Glory'

rows.label: Glory, praise, blessing, song, telling

not_verses.Lev.9.23: בָּרַךְ here is Moses and Aaron blessing the people
not_verses.Esth.5.11: סָפַר here is Haman recounting his own wealth

rows.label: Suffering and glory; called, destined, prepared in advance, brought to glory; the body raised in glory
rows.note: The verses that name it, as written. Where Christian traditions part on who is called and on what that rests, the page takes no side; the label uses only the text's own verbs and nouns (Rom 9:23 'prepared in advance for glory', 1 Cor 2:7 'destined for our glory').
rows._why: by hand, merged from 'Suffering and glory' (10), 'Called to glory, brought into glory, prepared for glory' (10) and 'Glory, the body, being raised' (5; 1 Cor 15:40 stayed in the splendor row below, the glory of the heavenly bodies is not a raising). Each verse has suffering, a verb of calling, bringing, destining or preparing, or a raising with glory as its end. Rom 9:23 ('prepared in advance for glory') is the verse where the dispute on election is sharpest

rows.label: Glory with hope, riches, grace, salvation, the throne, the kingdom

not_verses.Eph.1.17: 'riches' is the next verse's (1:18, 'the riches of His glorious inheritance')
not_verses.2Cor.8.19: χάρις there is the 'gracious offering', the collection, not grace as God's

rows._why: merged from 'Glory with hope, riches, grace and salvation' (22) and 'Glory and the throne, the kingdom' (14): a companion word in the verse

rows.label: Honor, wealth, riches, “my soul”: the same Hebrew word in another sense, not glory
rows.note: The Hebrew כָּבוֹד (from the root 'be heavy') is also rendered honor, wealth and riches, and at Ps 30:12 and 108:1 the original-language data glosses it 'soul' (the Berean prints 'heart' and 'being'). These are not the glory of God; they are listed so the word's other uses are seen and not mistaken for this sense.
rows._why: panel fix: the merged row of 63 is two rows again. This is the first kind: the word in another sense, glossed honor, wealth, riches, nobles or soul in the original-language data (44 verses). Ps 57:8 moved out (the Berean prints 'Awake, my glory!'; it is sense_keep, with glory). Ps 16:9, glossed glory, and Acts 22:11, glossed brightness, are in the next row. Ps 30:12 and 108:1 stay here: the original-language data glosses them 'soul', not glory

rows.label: The glory word where the Berean prints another word: splendor, pomp, praise, honor
rows.note: Here the original word is the glory word (Hebrew כָּבוֹד or Greek δόξα, glossed 'glory' in the original-language data) and the English chose another: 'splendor', 'pomp', 'honored', 'honor', 'brilliance'; at Gen 49:6, Isa 14:18 and Ps 16:9 the Berean prints no such word ('my tongue' at Ps 16:9). At Acts 22:11 the data glosses δόξα 'brightness'. Isa 16:14, 17:4, John 12:43 and 1 Thess 2:6, which are the same, are in the people row.
rows._why: panel fix, second of the two rows: 'glory by another name', 15 verses. Isa 16:14, Isa 17:4, John 12:43 and 1 Thess 2:6 were here and also in the people row; they are only in the people row now so no verse sits in both. The first four examples print splendor, pomp, honored (Isa 8:7, 10:18, Luke 14:10, Isa 10:16). Acts 22:11 is the panel's placing (the data says brightness, the Berean brilliance)

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Among them 2 Cor 3:7, 3:9, 3:10 and 3:11 (and 3:8, which is listed under the Holy Spirit). They set the glory of Moses' ministry, whose face the Israelites could not gaze at (Exodus 34:29-35), beside the glory of the ministry of the Spirit and of righteousness, as the text has them; the page does not say what this implies for the Law or for Israel, and readers part on that.
rows._why: what no row above takes (29 before the panel); 2 Cor 3:7, 3:9-11 are folded here and led first so they are seen (panel: findable); the note names 3:8's row and the Exod 34 context the text itself supplies

rows.label: Jesus glorified: the Father glorifies the Son, the Son glorifies the Father
rows.note: John 16:14 says 'He will glorify Me'; the sentence before names the Spirit of truth, and the page says no more than the verses do.
rows._why: by hand: verses where the text names the Father (or God) and the Son glorifying each other, and Jesus glorified. Panel round: the two rows 'Father glorifies the Son; the Son the Father' (9) and 'Jesus glorified' (10) are one row again to hold the total at 26 after the split of the other-sense rows and the John 17 prayer row; every verse is still labelled by whom the text names

rows.label: Glorify God (Greek δοξάζω)
rows._why: by hand: the object is God or the Father in the verse; Rom 1:21 is 'neither glorified Him as God', the not-doing stands with the doing as the text has it. Kept apart from the Hebrew row: different words

rows.label: Glorify or honor the LORD, the LORD gains glory (Hebrew כָּבֵד, sometimes printed honor)
rows._why: Hebrew, by hand, apart from the Greek row above. Panel fix: Ps 22:23 and Isa 25:3 print 'honor' (the same verb, kept only where it is glorify; 'honor your father' is the sense the rule leaves out), so the label says so

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Among them Rom 8:30 and Acts 13:48, which speak of those predestined, called and appointed; Christian traditions part on who is meant and on what that rests, and the page takes no side. And 2 Cor 3:10, which sets the glory of the two ministries side by side as the text has them (see the note at the noun row 'Every other use'); the page does not say what this implies for the Law or for Israel.
rows._why: includes the verb rows folded in: the name and the word glorified (8 verses: Deut 28:58 is the participle 'glorious', not an act of glorifying) and 'those He called, He also glorified' (Rom 8:30, 8:17, side by side without a reading of when or how)
